- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or use mean reversion to prior 5-day average.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) within 3–5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility — dampen forecast by 10–15% for next 3–5 periods.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in downward trends — if price drops >5% from recent high, forecast should not fall below 3–4% below prior low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum — if sentiment is trending upward, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% per sentiment unit above 0.5.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model tends to “smooth” extremes — avoid averaging; instead, use sentiment-weighted median or exponential decay filter for recent 7-day window.
